column2: On the authority of Abū Najīḥ al-ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriyah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave us an admonition at which our hearts trembled and our eyes shed tears. We said: “O Messenger of Allah, it is as though this were a farewell admonition, so advise us.”

He said: “I advise you to fear Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and to hear and obey, even if a slave is put in command over you. For whoever of you lives will see much disagreement. So hold to my Sunnah and the Sunnah of the rightly guided caliphs;
bite onto it with your molar teeth. And beware of newly invented matters, for every innovation is misguidance.” Reported by Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, who said: A ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
The printed text reads وجفت, evidently for وجلت (“trembled”).

Waʿaẓanā (“gave us an admonition”): counselled and reminded us. Mawʿiẓatan (“an admonition”): its tanwīn is to magnify its importance. Wajilat (“trembled”): feared intensely. Minhā (“at it”): because of it.
Dharafat (“shed tears”): flowed with tears. “To hear and obey”: those in authority. “Hold to my Sunnah”: my way; keep to it and hold fast to it.

“Whoever of you lives”: whoever lives long, or remains after me. Al-rāshidīn (“the rightly guided”): those who knew the truth and followed it, namely Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān and ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with them).

“Bite onto it with your molar teeth (al-nawājidh)”: the rearmost molars; what is meant is emphasis on holding fast to the Sunnah. Bidʿah (“innovation”): what is introduced without evidence from the Sharīʿah. Ḍalālah (“misguidance”): ruin.
Being intense in admonition, because it softens hearts and makes them receptive to the truth.
Relying on contextual indications in some situations.
One should ask the admonisher for more admonition and warning.
Among the signs of prophethood is his ﷺ foretelling the disagreement that would occur in his nation after him; and it happened as he ﷺ foretold.
The command to fear Allah the Exalted and to hear and obey those in authority, even if they are slaves, as long as they do not command disobedience; [this is said] to emphasise obeying them.
Holding fast to the Sunnah and bearing patiently the harm that befalls the one who holds fast to it.
A warning against innovating matters that have no basis in the Sharīʿah.
The honour and virtue of the rightly guided caliphs, and following their Sunnah.

This hadith tells that the Messenger ﷺ one day gave his Companions an admonition at which tears flowed from their eyes and their hearts feared intensely, because of its strong effect on their souls and because of what stirred in their breasts that it was the admonition of one bidding farewell to the people of this world; so they asked him for further advice.
He advised them to fear Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, which is Allah's counsel to the first and the last; to hear and obey those in authority; and to hold fast to his Sunnah

and the Sunnah of the rightly guided caliphs, and to hold it as firmly as possible, by every means; and not to follow the opinions of the people of innovation, whims and corrupt aims, for whoever follows them has gone astray and lost.
Among what has been said about taqwā:
If a man does not put on the garments of piety, / he is stripped naked, even if he is clothed.
The best of a man's qualities is obedience to his Lord, / and there is no good in one who disobeys Allah.
Another poet:
So hold to the fear of Allah, cling to it and you will succeed; / the God-fearing one is the radiant, the revered.
